title: Semi-Supervised Noise Adaptation: Transferring Knowledge from Noise Domain
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Meaningless synthetic noise classes can be mapped one-to-one onto target classes, letting knowledge flow from the noise domain to the target.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, shared class-index ellipse on top with colored arrows
description: The figure has two boxed panels side by side. The left panel is labeled Noise Domain and the right panel is labeled Target Domain. A bold hollow arrow marked Knowledge points from left to right between them. The left box holds two overlapping blobs, one purple and one blue. Dotted arrows lead from sample points in each blob to gray static-noise rectangles with purple and blue borders. The right box holds one irregular blue-to-purple blob. Dotted arrows lead from its points to a puppy photo with a blue border and a kitten photo with a purple border. At the top, an ellipse labeled Class Index Set contains the labels 0 and 1. Purple and blue curved arrows run from the noise patches and from the animal photos to those labels. This shows the one-to-one class correspondence. The eye goes first to the photos and the ellipse.
caption: Semi-Supervised Noise Adaptation (SSNA): The target domain includes a limited number of labeled samples, with most remaining unlabeled, while the noise domain is generated from random distributions. Noise classes, lacking semantic meaning, are mapped one-to-one to target classes. The goal is to improve the generalization of the target domain by utilizing the noise domain.
abstract: Transfer learning aims to facilitate the learning of a target domain by transferring knowledge from a source domain. The source domain typically contains semantically meaningful samples (*e.g.*, images) to facilitate effective knowledge transfer. However, a recent study observes that the noise domain constructed from simple distributions (*e.g.*, Gaussian distributions) can serve as a surrogate source domain in the semi-supervised setting, where only a small proportion of target samples are labeled while most remain unlabeled. Based on this surprising observation, we formulate a novel problem termed *Semi-Supervised Noise Adaptation* (SSNA), which aims to leverage a synthetic noise domain to improve the generalization of the target domain. To address this problem, we first establish a generalization bound characterizing the effect of the noise domain on generalization, based on which we propose a Noise Adaptation Framework (NAF). Extensive experiments demonstrate that NAF effectively leverages the noise domain to tighten the generalization bound of the target domain, leading to improved performance. The codes are available at https://github.com/AIResearch-Group/SSNA.
